definition: Training on evaluation data, yielding inflated scores. The archived sources establish that for reasoning models it is both consequential and hard to detect, and they now divide into two responses. On detection: contamination introduced during supervised fine-tuning is detectable until a brief GRPO run conceals the signals detectors rely on, with PPO-style importance sampling and clipping identified as the cause, so a broad class of RL methods launders the evidence; and re-instantiating the same problems with different constants collapses RL-trained models by 20-95% on a strict metric. On construction, three newer benchmarks respond by making contamination structurally impossible rather than detectable — parameterized symbolic templates with executable ground truth, automated contamination-resistant generation with controllable difficulty, and symbolic variabilization of existing competition sets. A fourth use inverts it into a control: one source reports its largest effect on AIME 2025 specifically because that split postdates the base model's training cutoff.

evidence.note: Casts benchmark contamination auditing as sparse-mixture detection, proves that detectability is governed by the single quantity alpha*rho*sqrt(m), and shows empirically that the resulting power predictions transport while the sample-size budgets derived from them do not.
evidence.title: When Is Benchmark Contamination Detectable? Information Limits and Power-Calibrated Audits

evidence.note: A financial reasoning benchmark built from parameterized symbolic templates with executable Python, giving machine-verifiable step-level ground truth and contamination-free regeneration.
evidence.title: FinChain: A Symbolic Benchmark for Verifiable Chain-of-Thought Financial Reasoning

evidence.note: A business-domain benchmark pairing four knowledge areas with three practitioner roles, designed to trace application performance back to the theoretical capability it depends on.
evidence.title: BizCompass: Benchmarking the Reasoning Capabilities of LLMs in Business Knowledge and Applications

evidence.note: An inductive-reasoning benchmark from historical linguistics that requires inducing cascades of string-rewrite programs, with automated contamination-resistant generation and controllable difficulty.
evidence.title: PBEBench: A Multi-Step Programming by Examples Reasoning Benchmark inspired by Historical Linguistics

evidence.note: Shows that benchmark contamination in reasoning models is alarmingly easy to hide: a brief round of GRPO erases the signals contamination detectors rely on, and PPO-style importance sampling and clipping are identified as the cause — implying a broad class of RL methods conceals contamination inherently.
evidence.title: On The Fragility of Benchmark Contamination Detection in Reasoning Models

evidence.note: Converts AMC23 and AIME24/25 into symbolic templates whose constants are replaced by sampled variables, requires a model to solve several instantiations of each problem, and finds RL-finetuned models lose most of their reported accuracy under that consistency requirement.
evidence.title: VAR-MATH: Probing True Mathematical Reasoning in LLMs via Symbolic Multi-Instance Benchmarks

evidence.note: Shows that base models win pass@K on mathematics by producing wrong chains that land on right answers, and that scoring the chain too — CoT-Pass@K — reverses the verdict in RLVR's favour at every K.
evidence.title: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards Implicitly Incentivizes Correct Reasoning in Base LLMs

name: benchmark contamination
